reuse.why: Builds on the tree's existing WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay abstraction: getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and schedule-template all route through it, and holidays go through one isNonWorkingDay.

duplication.why: getNextDate re-encodes the daily skip rule itself (isDailySchedule + filter on isNonWorkingDay + skipWeekend && !skipsWeekendDays) parallel to the daily branch inside applyWeekendRule, and the config-to-WeekendRule mapping is repeated in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Rule logic is in shared/schedules.ts and handlers only map fields and filter by range; the only misplacement is the separate daily decision inside getNextDate.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps, with a gratuitous import reorder in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: Most callers depend on one rule function, so holiday/daily changes mostly land in one place, though getNextDate's own daily path and the isDailySchedule vs rule.frequency==='daily' checks must be kept in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getNextDate decides daily skipping via isDailySchedule/firstWeekday filter and suppresses applyWeekendRule with !skipsWeekendDays instead of letting applyWeekendRule (which now knows frequency) decide.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily 'drop non-working days' rule appears in applyWeekendRule and again reshaped as the firstWeekday filter plus isDailySchedule in getNextDate.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gained frequency and holidays fields and getDateWithSkippedWeekend a holidays parameter; applyWeekendRule gained a daily special-case branch (returning null); getNextDate re-implements the daily decision instead of delegating.
